LVS.is - Shopify Development Proposal

Client: Laine Veide (lvs.is), beauty salon and online shop in Reykjavík
Prepared by: LitOS/LitGroup  ·  Date: October 12, 2026

You asked whether we can move lvs.is to Shopify and give you a first estimate, without admin access. This proposal is based on the public site only. It covers what we'd build, what we'd adjust, what is quoted separately, and what we still need from you.

1

Where you are today

lvs.is is a custom-built site in Icelandic. It is a salon site first: sugaring, hair, nails, brows and lashes, facials, each with a price list and a "BÓKA TÍMA" button that opens Noona booking. The shop sells sugaring products (Radeq Lab), Lycon SPA body care, niche perfume decants (2, 3, 5 and 10 ml), professional hair care (Olaplex, Kérastase, Kevin Murphy), wool slippers and gift cards.

The shop is the part that gets lost. Products appear as a few cards and banners between long service texts, and the shop pages have filters in several places.

2

Adjustments we recommend

We replicate your current site on Shopify and make targeted adjustments to improve the shopping experience. This is not a redesign. The aim is two clear paths: buy products, or book a service, with a refined, simple look suited to beauty products and perfume.

AreaWhat we see todayWhat we'd do
HomepageMostly services, long text, few products (§2.1)Shop and booking as two clear paths. Product sections on top. Service detail moves to its own pages.
HeaderNot fixed when you scroll (§2.2)Sticky header with menu, cart, search and "BÓKA TÍMA"
FooterServices list and a plain newsletter box (§2.3)Add a Shop column, restyle the newsletter

2.1 Homepage

The page reads like a landing page for the salon. We would put the shop first: featured products, brands, perfume decants and gift cards. Each service group (sugaring, hair, nails, brows and lashes, facials) gets its own page with its price list and a "BÓKA TÍMA" button. The homepage keeps a short block per service that links to that page.

2.2 Header and menu

TodayThe header scrolls away with the page (red arrows). We'd make it sticky so cart, search and booking are always in reach.

TodayMobile menu: eight items in one list, with "BÓKA TÍMA" and social icons at the bottom. We'd keep it short, with Shop and Services as the main entries.

2.3 Footer

TodayThe red boxes mark the newsletter and the empty space beside the services list. We'd add a "Shop" column and restyle the sign-up.

2.4 Contact page

TodayThe map and form take a full section of the homepage. We'd move them to a Contact page and leave only a link on the homepage.

2.5 Mobile slider

TodayThe "VERSLUN" button sits on top of the line "endurnærandi lúxus hárumhirða". We'd fix the space between text and button on every slide.

2.6 Collection page (desktop)

TodayFilters are split between the top box (sort, brand, category, price) and the sidebar (categories). The cart and search box on the right (crossed out) go away: the header already has both.

We'd put all filters in one place and add a hover effect on product cards, with "Add to cart" and "Quick view" icons. You can choose the filter layout: a bar on top like the reference below, a sidebar, or a popup that opens from a "Filter" button.

ReferenceAnother store's filter bar (fashion products, not LVS content). All filters in one row, each as a dropdown. We'd use the same pattern with your filters: price, brand, category, availability.

2.7 Collection page (mobile)

TodayThe filters fill the first screens before any product shows. On mobile we'd show a "Filter" button that opens a popup.

TodayEach card has wide side padding, so images are small. We'd reduce the gaps between columns.

TodayCard detail: the padding around the card and the image leaves little room for the title. We'd tighten it. Sizes such as "250ml" stay as variants.

2.8 Product page

We'd remove the sidebar and move "Tengdar vörur" (related products) below the product. Products that need size information get a "Size guide" link that opens a popup. The brief also mentions "buy together" bundles and loyalty points. Both need paid apps, so they are an open question (§4) and not in the estimate.

3

Migration and booking

3.1 Data migration

Products, collections, variants, images, customers, orders, SEO data and URL redirects are moved with LitExtension, our migration partner. LitExtension quotes this separately, based on your catalog size, and you buy it from them directly. We check the result in your store.

Limit: customer passwords can't be moved to Shopify. Customers get an email to set a new password the first time they log in.

3.2 Booking

"BÓKA TÍMA" stays and opens Noona, as it does today. We add it to the sticky header, the service pages and the mobile menu. Noona itself is your account and isn't changed.

5

Theme

We recommend Ella from HaloThemes. It is free to you through our partnership. It includes the sticky header, product card hover actions, filter layouts, quick view and size guide popup that §2 asks for. We adjust colors, fonts and spacing to fit your brand.

7

Who configures what

Payment and shipping are set up by you in your Shopify admin. We guide you and verify the result, but we don't enter the credentials. They give access to your money and your carrier rates, so they stay with the account holder.

ItemYou doWe do
Payment providerOpen the account, enter the credentials, run the first live orderRecommend a provider that works in Iceland, give you a step-by-step guide, test checkout
Shipping & pickupEnter zones and rates, keep them up to dateTurn your terms (free over 15,000 ISK, salon pickup) into a rate sheet, walk you through it, test real addresses
